steps.content: Goddess, please keep my parents healthy! Keep them safe and well on the mountain!
Goddess, I learned how to weave grasshoppers from grass blades now. Can you bring my brother back to see?
Sun Crow Goddess, please make me stronger and more capable! I want to go to the mountain. I want to protect our town!
Goddess...
Sun Crow Goddess...
Yao jerks awake, her heart hammering in her chest.
All around her stretch countless prayer ribbons, some already neatly sorted, others still waiting for her touch. Each one bears lines of tightly packed wishes, identical to those that fill her dream.

steps.speaker: Yao
steps.content: I will... hold your prayers close to my heart.
In your sleep, you seem to catch the sound of Yao's voice, softly murmuring a name. It is a tender sight, one that wears an expression she has never once glimpsed on your face.

steps.speaker: Yao
steps.content: Thank you... for yesterday.
Yao looks up at the tower that is now standing several stories higher, and a trace of exasperation crosses her face.
It is a blessing that both of you can wield your powers. Without them, who knows how long this tower might drag on.
The Bureau will hold a New Year gathering soon. She has to wrap everything up before then and get you back in time to join...
Whoa, no way! The Sun Crow Goddess actually lives here?!
The unexpected voice pulls Yao from her thoughts. Her gaze lifts to the doorway, where a tall, slender boy staggers under an armload of wood, poised with one foot already crossing into the tower.

steps.speaker: Yao
steps.content: Ah... this place is... it has its charms, yes.

steps.speaker: Yao
steps.content: Ahem... But what brings you here?

steps.speaker: Yao
steps.content: I told you before. There's no need for any of you to come build this tower.
At Yao's words, the boy's brow creases in clear unease. He lowers the lumber to the ground and brushes his palms clean.

steps.speaker: Boy
steps.content: Yeah, well... my ma always says, you work hard, you earn your keep. Don't be the kinda person who just takes and takes.

steps.speaker: Boy
steps.content: I know I'm all gangly and awkward. Too tall, balance is shot. I ain't built like my pa is. He can go up the mountain and keep folks safe.

steps.speaker: Boy
steps.content: But just sitting around, letting the goddess protect me and not doing anything for it... that just doesn't sit right. Y'know?
The boy slips his hands into his sleeves and sinks into a crouch by the threshold, averting his face in a flush of embarrassment.

steps.speaker: Boy
steps.content: I still got some muscle in me. I can help with the tower...

steps.speaker: Yao
steps.content: ...Sigh.
A gentle sigh escapes Yao, and she regards the boy with a warm smile.

steps.speaker: Yao
steps.content: I see now.

steps.speaker: Yao
steps.content: But tell me... do the others feel this way too?
The boy freezes for a moment before spinning around to follow Yao's gesture. A cluster of residents peeks from around the door, their heads craning as they listen in on the exchange.

steps.speaker: Villager A
steps.content: He's right, he's right! That's what I've been thinking this whole time!

steps.speaker: Villager B
steps.content: I still got some strength left in me too, y'know!

steps.speaker: Villager C
steps.content: Yeah, it doesn't sit right with me either! Let us help build the tower for the Sun Crow Goddess!

steps.speaker: Boy
steps.content: H-hey—wait, wait, wait! What're you all—?! Quit saying that stuff!!
The boy shoots upright and plows through the cluster of residents in a flustered rush, his cheeks blazing a deep red.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Mmh... what's with all the noise...
Still dragging yourself from sleep, you catch only the noise of a heated commotion nearby. The question slips from your lips before you can stop it.
To your surprise, the voices die at once. That sudden stillness jolts you alert. You force your eyes open and slap lightly at your cheeks to chase away the drowsiness.
What you find then is Yao and a cluster of people mid-argument by the tower entrance, all of them frozen in place as if time itself has stopped, every gaze fixed squarely on you.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Uh... morning?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You could've... woken me up sooner.

The heat of embarrassment still lingers in your ears. You grab a wooden plank and pass it to the boy beside you, who fastens it to the hoist rope and hauls it upward to the residents working at the tower's top.

steps.speaker: Yao
steps.content: Forgive me. You seemed so tired... I thought it best to let you rest a little longer.

steps.speaker: Yao
steps.content: The shackles... they weigh on you, too.
A sheepish smile tugs at your lips. Yao has a point: within Yugu's tale, the shackles serve as a tool you can actually wield.
Yet here, their power takes on the cast of divine miracle, only deepening the residents' conviction that you and Yao truly are the envoy and the goddess.
Rumble!!
A low growl of thunder rolls across the distance, and every hand stills. You lift your gaze to the horizon and realize the heavy bank of storm clouds has edged closer, unnoticed until now.

steps.speaker: Boy
steps.content: It's... it's getting closer again... ain't it?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Don't worry. We're here with you.
You move closer and give the boy's hair an affectionate ruffle before passing him the wooden plank once more. Your words seem to lift his spirits. He gives a resolute nod and turns back to his task.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Good thing they showed up to help on their own. Those clouds are moving fast... Looks like it won't be long before the whole town's swallowed up.

steps.speaker: Yao
steps.content: Yes. That's why I couldn't bring myself to send them away.

steps.speaker: Yao
steps.content: After all... if they had no will to act, no fire of their own, only empty prayers...
Yao gestures toward the little bird that keeps bouncing about at the residents' side.

The creature bears little resemblance to the round, downy ball it once was. Now it perches steady on three legs, its wings flared open to reveal sharply defined feathers, each one stretching nearly the length of her forearm.

steps.speaker: Yao
steps.content: Look. Its wings have grown strong, full and ready. It's time...

steps.speaker: Yao
steps.content: ...that it learns to spread its wings and fly.

steps.speaker: Boy
steps.content: Left! Little more left! Ah, too far! Back right a bit!
The final rooftop ornament rises slowly to the tower's peak. Once it rests where it belongs, the long labor reaches its end.
You and Yao leave the boy to guide the placement of that last piece. Following his steady direction, the rooftop beast sinks at last into its rightful seat.

steps.speaker: Boy
steps.content: Perfect! It's perfect! Goddess! Quick, you gotta get up your tower and see for yourself!
Rumble!!!
Yet just as the tower nears its final form, the dark clouds press inward—hunters ringing their quarry—and threaten to swallow the town whole.
Yao spares no breath to answer the boy's invitation. Side by side with you, she herds the townsfolk back toward the safety of their doors.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Listen, stay inside your homes. Don't leave until we say so, got it?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: And get word to anyone keeping watch on the mountain. Tell them to come down now. Head home if they can make it; if not, find somewhere safe and hunker down.
Flustered and unsure, the boy lingers where he stands. When he finally moves to go, he discovers his fingers have been clutching the hem of Yao's robe all along, refusing to release their grip.

steps.speaker: Yao
steps.content: Don't be afraid. Trust in us. We promised we would keep you safe.

steps.speaker: Yao
steps.content: And besides... this tower does not belong to me alone.
Yao gently eases the boy's grip free from her robe and taps the back of his hand.

steps.speaker: Yao
steps.content: It belongs to all of us. It's... our tower.
